_what: Settings for do-work/trillion.mjs (moved from Trillion-X/trillion harness/trillion.json), the `trillion` command any AI with a shell runs to see the person's AIs and their AI jobs, run their Workshop tools and hand and take work. Every command is one call of the engine's one MCP tool `engine.tool` (run_resource_operation {address, method, request_key, input}) at the account's door; nothing here decides work. The door is the Mac app's local door when the app `mac_app` names declares one on this computer (local-door.mjs reads its computer-reader.json and private adoption descriptor), else `origin`; --origin or TRILLION_ORIGIN name one. whoami reads the account from MCP initialize (`engine.account_meta` in result._meta). `engine` names what the engine serves: `records` (records:read and records:write of this AI's own `ai_type` record, records:history of a job) and `tools` (the Workshop tools:list and tools:run), and how many pages a list may take. `work` is the one table of the AI-job commands: each names the Workshop work tool (tools/hand-work-to-ais) that does it, and a claim is that tool's conditioned write, never one made here. `words` are every refusal: a refusal names the door, and only `no_credential` and `sign_in_ended` say to log in. The account key is the existing one: the Keychain item `keychain_item` the Trillion Mac app keeps, or, where there is no Keychain, `key_file` (0600). With no key, `login` signs in once in the browser (OAuth with PKCE to a loopback address at `origin`) and keeps that sign-in (access and refresh tokens) in the Keychain item `grant.keychain_item`, or the 0600 file `grant.file` in `state_folder`; it is renewed at /oauth/token `grant.refresh_before_seconds` before it ends and is used at the public door. `who` shows the AIs tool:see-my-ais answers that were seen within `who.seen_within_days` (all of them with --all), grouped by owner (the record's `owner`, else the account the door answers for; yours first) and then by name, one line per AI with its ready chats beneath (every chat with --all), and says how many it hid; liveness is the tool's, computed when read, never stored. An AI's name is the formula title field of the person's list `who.ai_list`, evaluated by `who.formula_tool` over the stored values in one call; it is never built or stored here, and a missing list is said by name. `install` is where `setup` copies this program and the link it puts on PATH. `skills` are the instruction files `setup` writes for each AI app, one row per app: `folder` under the home folder (or `home_variable`), the file under it, and `detect` (paths whose presence says the app is on this computer). `agents` name the AI running the command from its environment; `session_env` are the variables that app sets to one value per chat session, in order (Claude Code sets CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, Codex sets CODEX_THREAD_ID; the Cursor agent sets only CURSOR_AGENT=1 for its commands, so a Cursor chat has no session and keeps the computer id). `agent_id` builds the id: `session` when a session variable is set (its last `session_chars` letters and digits, the random end of a UUID v4 or v7), else `computer`; --as or TRILLION_AGENT replace it. `most_chars` is the longest agent id Trillion keeps (src/agents.mjs reads agent_id as trimmed text of at most 200 characters and cuts a longer one, so a longer one is refused here). A job taken under the computer id before sessions were added is still finished, released or said stuck under the id that took it (held.json says which). `agent_card` and `ai_record` shape this AI's own `ai` record, which publish writes conditioned on the value just read (a person's edit made meanwhile is kept), facts only: `owner` the account the door answered for, `app` and `model` from the running app's `agents` row (`model_env`, else the setting `model_config` names in the app's own config file, with `model_suffix` removed), `provider` from the model's family (else the row's), `computer` the computer's own name (`computer_name`: the system program per platform, with the duplicate counter `strip` removes), `where` the repository (the last part of the origin remote, else the top folder's name) and branch, and `working_on` the title of the job it holds (`working_on`, `working_on_more`) or null. `live.seen_at` is set to now on every write, and serve writes it again every `serve.contact_seconds`. `send_note` is what `send` says about when the receiver sees the job.

recipes.label: Any program that sends HTTP
recipes.template: POST {mcp_url} with the header Authorization: Bearer ${key_env}

recipes.label: Any AI with a shell
recipes.template: trillion setup  (then: trillion call TOOL JSON)

retry._what: One call is tried again, under the same request_key, when the door does not answer within one try, answers 429 or 5xx, or says its run is still going (`codes`). A call has no deadline of its own: `count`, the number of tries after the first, is the one number that ends it. Each gap doubles from first_seconds up to most_seconds and is then cut down by up to `jitter` of itself, so callers that failed together do not try together. `attempt_seconds` is how long one try waits (--timeout SECONDS sets it for one command); the next try asks again with the same key and is answered with the first run's recorded result (trillion-rust tool_runs: one request key, one run). A run longer than the engine's tool-run deadline (tool-runs.json deadline_ms) is a row that declares invoke.max_run_ms or invoke.session, whose run id is read with the session read method.

direct_calls._what: The flags `trillion op` and `trillion call` take, per command; any other flag is refused before anything is sent (parseArgs makes every unknown --flag a true, so an unchecked one was silently dropped: `op ... records:write --dry-run` removed a record on 2026-11-13). `--dry-run` is op only: it prints the request it would have sent {address, method, request_key, input} and sends nothing, except that for `dry_run_reads_first.method` (records:write) it reads each target row with `read_method` and prints, per row, the current value, the new value, a field-by-field diff, the fields the write drops, and `removes` for a value null; no write is sent.

dry_run_reads_first.no_validate_route: This engine does not say it can check a write without committing it (initialize capabilities.experimental.records_write_check_only), so this preview cannot say whether the engine would refuse the write.
dry_run_reads_first.not_honored: THE ENGINE DID NOT HONOR check_only: its answer is not a check, so the write may have been applied. Read the rows.

follow._what: Where the installed command finds the Workshop copy it runs: the first of runtime_files that exists names the engine's state folder in `state_field`; <state>/<installs_folder>/<current> is the Workshop install the engine keeps current (current is `current_field` of <state>/<installs_folder>/<state_file>), and `program` is the command inside it. Nothing found, or the copy is this file: the installed copy runs itself.

agent_card.where_in_repository: repository {repository}, branch {branch}, in a terminal on this computer

send_note.any: Any of your AIs can take it. An AI in a terminal sees it the next time it runs trillion work or trillion take, or at once while trillion serve runs there; an AI app sees it when it next reads its Trillion work.
send_note.to: {to} sees it the next time it runs trillion work or trillion take, or at once while trillion serve runs for it.

update.workshop: The installed trillion command follows the Workshop: each run it finds the Workshop copy this computer's engine has installed (install.follow) and runs that copy instead of itself, so a Workshop update reaches every command at once. `trillion setup` run from the Workshop copy also refreshes the installed files, which stay as the fallback when no Workshop copy is found. The command never fetches code by itself.

ag_ui._what: `trillion serve --ag-ui URL` (ag-ui-agent.mjs): any AG-UI agent at URL runs each job this AI takes. tools: the Trillion tools the agent is offered as AG-UI frontend tools; each call it makes of one is made by this program as this AI. max_turns: the most runs of the agent one job gets (each answered tool call starts the next). run_seconds: the longest one run is waited for. quiet_seconds: the longest the agent may send nothing while it is waited on (a silence watchdog; time spent running its tools here does not count). answer_chars: the most characters of a tool's answer given back to the agent. max_frame_chars and max_events bound what one run may send. context is the ambient line every run is given ({handoff_id}). words: what is recorded when something goes wrong, in plain words.
ag_ui.context: This is the person's job {handoff_id} in their Trillion. Your answer is recorded as its result. To use what is in their Trillion, call the tools you are given; each call is made as you, for this job.

words.interrupted: The AG-UI agent stopped to ask for something.
words.cancelled: The AG-UI agent cancelled its run.
words.no_words: The AG-UI agent finished without saying anything.
words.not_offered: {tool} is not a tool offered here. Use only the tools you were given.
words.too_many_turns: The AG-UI agent called tools for {turns} runs without answering, so the job was given back.

work._what: Each AI-job command runs one Workshop work tool (trillion-workshop tools/hand-work-to-ais) with tools:run at @workshop-tools: `tools` names the tool for who (ais), send, work (see), take and every move (change); `actions` maps a move command to the action tool:change-an-ai-job takes; `publish_after` are the commands after which this AI writes its own ai record again (what it holds changed, or it just sent work).

bearers._what: The shapes of credential the door accepts as a bearer, one row each: a `pattern` the whole value must match. The command sends whatever bearer it is given (TRILLION_KEY, the kept key, a key read on standard input) as it is, and refuses only a value no row matches, so a new kind of key or pass is one row here and no change in code. nm_ is the Mac app's account key; tr_ is a Better Auth API key (the prefix and 64 letters, no digits or separators, as the apiKey plugin mints it: better-auth-official, Nov 14); the third is an access token that is a signed JWT (three base64url parts).
bearers.refused: That is not a kind of key or token the door takes ({kinds}).

keep._what: Where a result too long for the job row is kept (keep-result.mjs): one file of the person's files, named {folder}/<job id>/result by the program, never by the caller; the job row's result then holds the `pointer` line. The inline limit is not here: it is the `maxLength` of the result input of the tool that finishes jobs, read from the door. piece_bytes is the account files' fixed span size (pages-32k-v1) a resumable upload takes at a time; read_bytes is how much one read asks for (the door answers at most its own most).
keep.pointer: Kept as file {name} ({bytes} bytes, {identity}). Read it whole: trillion work {id} --result

words.no_limit: The door states no most length for the result of {tool}, so nothing was kept or finished.
words.not_started: The upload of {name} did not start (state {state}); nothing was finished.
words.mismatch: {name} did not read back with the identity and size of the bytes sent; the job was not finished.
words.read_broken: {name} could not be read back whole and exact at byte {offset}.

words.unknown_flag: trillion {command} does not take --{flag}; it takes {known}. Nothing was sent.
words.no_credential: This computer has no Trillion key or sign-in. Run trillion login (or trillion setup) first.
words.sign_in_ended: This computer's sign-in to Trillion has ended. Run trillion login to sign in again.
words.refused_key_at_door: {door} does not admit this computer's key yet{local}.
words.local_door_named: ; the key works at this computer's local door {mcp}
words.no_account: {door} answered initialize without naming an account.
words.pager_stuck: {method} answered a page it already gave ({next}), so its pages would never end.
words.timeout_range: --timeout is a whole number of seconds, at least 1: how long one try waits before the next try.
words.no_answer: {door} did not answer after {tries} tries with the same request key.
words.byte_page_broken: {method} answered a byte_page that does not hold together ({why}), so its pages were not joined and nothing was answered.
words.byte_page_mismatch: {method} answered pages whose joined {bytes} bytes have BLAKE3 {got}, not the {want} the door named, so the answer was refused.
words.more_jobs: More jobs: trillion work --limit N, or --status, --to, --from, --taker.
words.sent_before: {id} was sent before; here it is as it now is.
words.nothing_to_take: No waiting job you may take.
words.not_moved: {id} was not moved ({reason}); here it is as it now is.
words.not_published: This AI's record was not written: {why}
words.not_finished: Not finished after {seconds} seconds; read it later with trillion work {id}.
words.retry_with_key: Ask again with {flag} {key}: the same key answers the call that was sent first, so it is not run twice.
words.request_key_line: Request key: {key} (quote it to ask again under the same key).
words.write_pending: The write to {method} was kept, but the person's records have not settled it yet. Read them again before answering again.

codes._what: Plain words for the engine refusal codes a person meets most; any other code is said with refused_code.
codes.workshop_tool_unknown: {tool} is not in this account's Workshop yet ({door}).
codes.original_command_conflict: The record changed meanwhile, so nothing was written ({door}).

who.no_name: An AI with no app, model or computer recorded ({kind})
who.hidden: {count} more chats not seen in {days} days; trillion who --all shows them.
who.none: No AI on this account was seen lately.
who.no_list: No list {list} names your AIs: its title field must be a formula field. Make the list, or ask Trillion to, and run trillion who again.
who.no_names: {tool} did not answer one name per AI.

ai_record._what: This AI's own ai record, written by publish through @own-records records:write conditioned on the value just read. A new record starts from `new`; `write_tries` writes are tried when another write changed it meanwhile (the engine answers one of `changed_codes`).
